subject: Clarify: commit aggregation, per-token rounding, and streaming metering
messages:
From: Sofia Morales <sofia.morales@acme.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: 2026-10-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Questions on commit tiers and streaming token billing

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement asked me to get clear on three contract items before we loop legal: 1) If we agree a quarterly commit (say 500M tokens), how are usage credits aggregated across different model families (e.g., small chat models vs. large LLMs)? Can we pool across models, or do commits attach to specific SKUs? 2) For streaming endpoints, do you bill per token as soon as the token is emitted (so partial tokens from in-flight streams get charged), and how do you round fractional billing units? 3) If we exceed the commit mid-quarter, is overage billed at an overage rate or do you pro-rate the next commit slab?

We're preparing an SOW and want the language to be tight — can you point me to suggested contract wording or a short redline? I've attached a draft SOW (Acme_SOW_v3.pdf).

Appreciate a concise reply so procurement can advise counsel.

Best,
Sofia
Procurement, Acme Corp

From: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
To: Sofia Morales <sofia.morales@acme.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-22T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on commit tiers and streaming token billing

Hi Sofia — thanks for the clear list. Looping Marcus (solutions) and Lauren (legal) to propose language and confirm runtime behavior. Quick answers up-front so procurement has something to work with:

- Commit aggregation: we support a single commit across all hosted API usage in the same account by default (i.e., credits are fungible across model SKUs). We can optionally restrict a commit to a model family if the customer requests a dedicated SKU commit (usually for reserved capacity deals).

- Streaming billing: tokens are metered when emitted by the service (server-side). For streaming, we bill per token with per-request granularity and then apply our rounding policy.

- Rounding and overage: the typical approach is per-token billing with rounding to the nearest token (no fractional-token charges). Overage within the billing period is billed at the agreed overage rate. We can discuss carry-forward or proration alternatives for enterprise deals.

Marcus and Lauren — attaching Acme_SOW_v3.pdf from Sofia. Can you each add a short suggested clause (text snippet) for: commit aggregation, streaming token measurement + rounding, and mid-period overage/proration? If legal prefers a redline doc I'll ask Ops to produce redline_commit_language.docx.

Thanks,
Jasmine
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
Cc: Sofia Morales <sofia.morales@acme.com>, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-23T08:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on commit tiers and streaming token billing

Hi all — technical notes to map to contract language:

1) Commit aggregation: We implement a single billing ledger per account ID. Credits are deducted from that ledger regardless of model variant (embedding/generation) unless the contract explicitly creates isolated ledgers (rare for hosted). If Acme wants model-isolated commits, we'll need a separate billing SKU and will likely require provisioning changes.

2) Streaming measurement: streaming responses emit token events as the model generates them. Metering occurs at generation time server-side. For interrupted streams (client disconnects or network drop), tokens already emitted are counted; incomplete tokens that were never emitted are not metered.

3) Rounding behavior: currently our pricing engine rounds to the next whole token per request (ceiling) for safety in billing. However enterprise deals sometimes specify rounding-to-nearest or per-request aggregation then round at daily granularity. We can support alternative rounding or aggregation windows but will need to confirm with billing on impact.

Suggested short snippet for SOW (draft):
"Commit aggregation: Customer commit is applied to the account-level usage ledger and is fungible across model SKUs unless otherwise specified in writing.

Streaming & metering: Tokens are metered when emitted by Redwood's hosted API. For streaming endpoints, tokens emitted in-flight prior to request termination are billable.

Rounding & overage: Usage is aggregated per request and rounded to the nearest billable token according to Redwood's billing policy. Usage exceeding committed tokens in the billing period will be invoiced at the agreed overage rate unless alternate proration or carry-forward terms are specified in the Order Form."

I'll attach a CSV sample of a streaming session (usage_sample.csv) so Acme can see event-level measurements.

— Marcus (Solutions)

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: Sofia Morales <sofia.morales@acme.com>
Date: 2026-10-27T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on commit tiers and streaming token billing

Hi team — I drafted contract language and flagged two points for commercial confirmation. I attached a redline (redline_commit_language.docx) but paste the critical clauses below for faster review. I've kept the drafting concise so Acme counsel can drop it into their SOW.

Proposed clauses (editable):
1) Commit Pooling: "Except as otherwise expressly set forth in the Order Form, Customer's committed usage shall be applied to a single account-level usage pool and shall be fungible across all Hosted API model SKUs provided under this Agreement. Redwood may, at Customer's request and subject to additional fees and provisioning timelines, allocate a portion of the committed usage to a dedicated SKU."

2) Streaming Token Metering: "For streaming endpoints, Redwood meters tokens upon emission by the service. Tokens that are emitted prior to legitimate request termination (including client disconnects, network interruptions, or cancelled requests) shall be billable. Tokens not emitted by the service are not billable."

3) Rounding and Billing Granularity: "Usage shall be measured at request-level granularity and rounded to the nearest whole token. Parties may agree in the Order Form to an alternative rounding or aggregation window (e.g., daily rounding) which shall be documented as an exhibit and may affect pricing calculations."

4) Overage and Proration: "If Customer's usage exceeds the committed amount within a billing period, Customer will be billed for overage at the rate set forth in the Order Form. Parties may agree in writing to allow carry-forward of unused commit or pro-rate future commit slabs; such arrangements must be set forth in the Order Form or an executed amendment."

Lauren's notes / commercial questions:
- Do we want to offer a default carry-forward (e.g., 10% unused carryforward) for this deal as a competitive sweetener? That changes revenue recognition and should be priced.
- If Acme requests model-specific commits, we should include a provisioning lead time and an initial setup fee.

I'll leave the redline doc attached for their counsel — happy to iterate quickly if Acme pushes back.

Thanks,
Lauren
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Sofia Morales <sofia.morales@acme.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acme.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-30T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on commit tiers and streaming token billing

Hi all — thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear snippets. Counsel reviewed Lauren's proposed clauses and had two small asks before we proceed to signatures:

1) Can you change the rounding language to "rounded down to the nearest whole token for streaming endpoints when the customer terminates the stream early" — our lawyers prefer consumers not be charged for tokens that may be partially emitted at the moment of disconnect. Can Redwood accommodate a rounding-down exception specifically for client-abort events?

2) For overage/proration: procurement prefers a soft-pro-rate where overage billing is applied at month-end but Acme can convert overage into additional commit credits at the next month start at the contract rate (no markup) — essentially an automatic commit top-up. Is that something Redwood supports? If not standard, what's the commercial impact?

If you can provide a one-paragraph response to these two points (and an updated one-paragraph clause for the SOW), procurement is ready to proceed to final DocuSign.

Best,
Sofia
Procurement, Acme Corp
